title: Drummers in Miller's own band and Paul Barber's trouble
summary: Chinese Foster, Arnal DePaz, Happy Goldston and Paul Barber, who left after trouble with white patrons over a woman.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You got it. Mm-hmm. So, let's see. You had different guys in your band, I know you had a lot of different drummers I know it told me.
Yeah, yeah, yeah, I couldn't keep regular drummers.
But I didn't have but two, three. China?

Three. Three. Arnel Matoyer. What's his name? Arnel? No, Arnal something. A little short, short fella, a stomach on him like that. Tell me he's a policy writer now. He's downtown. Arnal. Arnal. But not Matoyer there, that was a trumpet player. Yeah. But he named Arnal DePaz.
Oh, I didn't know he was downtown.
Yeah, DePaz, Arnal DePaz. Well, but he wasn't my first drummer. See, Chinese kept on messing up and I used to have to go like the devil and get somebody, see.
Yeah, he used to blow me up a lot of times. But I tell you who played me a long time, Happy Goldston. He took Chinese plays, see. I kept him when I got him. That's before he went to the tuxedo.
Well, Chinese was with the tuxedo.
Chinese was a good drummer, but Chinese would get high like that and mess you up, man.
Did Paul Barber never play with you? Well, yeah.
Paul Barber, I don't want to tell that to him. Paul Barber, yeah, when he first came back from Lewis he joined me.
I thought maybe he played with you in those days, in years gone by. Before? Yeah, with Eddie Marsh and George E. Bush.

Yeah, that's when he played with me. That's when he played with me, before I ever left here. He had been to Chicago with Lewis and he said something, he got slow in his foot or something, I don't know what was wrong. But he left Chicago and come here, see. And he joined my band and played with me. Until one night we was playing with some white boys back, way back off Porter Street. Back, I believe Galvis, somewhere around that day. And Paul must have thought he was still up north, you know, trying to flag them girls, see. But I said the boy was watching him. They all knowed me, them white boys. So they called me outside. He said, you better tell that drummer something or you get hype. I said, what's the matter? He said, well, he's, one girl said that he told her he'd gone for a big way and all that old kind of stuff, you know. So they're fixing to get off all that night, see. So what I did, I told him, I said, well you all leave him alone, I bet you don't buy nobody anymore. So I told him about it and he quit that night and then I got gold stuck with me. I said, I got gold stuck with me. Yeah, that man felt fixing to mess up man, completely.
But he know it better, yeah.
But he just thought he could get by with it. He know it better.
Excuse me, but I've been all over the country and nothing like that was with me. So I always, nowhere up long, be there. I never let nothing like that was with me.
